facts.statement: The genus Watsonosteus was described by Miles and Westoll in 1963.
The type species of the genus is Watsonosteus fletti, originally described by Watson in 1932.
Watsonosteus lived during the Late Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period.
facts.quote: Late Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period

facts.statement: Fossils of Watsonosteus date from 387.95 to 382.31 million years ago.
facts.quote: Givetian to Givetian (387.95 to 382.31 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Watsonosteus have been found in the Orkney Islands, Scotland.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Orkney Islands, Scotland

facts.statement: Watsonosteus was a small placoderm measuring 57 cm on average, with the largest individuals reaching 1 meter in length.
facts.quote: It was a small placoderm with a total body length of 57 cm, with the largest individuals reaching lengths of 1 m

facts.statement: Watsonosteus is one of the few arthrodire genera known from complete body fossils.
facts.quote: It is one of the few arthrodires for which complete body fossils are known

facts.statement: Watsonosteus is classified as an extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm.
facts.quote: extinct genus of coccosteid arthrodire placoderm

facts.statement: Watsonosteus belongs to the family Coccosteidae, which is part of the clade Coccosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: member of the family Coccosteidae, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci

facts.statement: Watsonosteus is classified in the class Placodermi.
